FN-L817WAW-1
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 309
Committee: Ways and Means General Fund Sponsor: Representative Ginny Shaver
Analyst: John Friedenreich Date: 03/18/2024
House Bill 309 as introduced would decrease the potential savings of select state entities by an
estimated maximum of $8,600 per employee that utilizes eight weeks of paid leave for the birth
or adoption of a child, pursuant to the provisions of this bill, and who otherwise would have
utilized unpaid leave. This bill would also provide that the parental leave provided would not
require the use of any accrued personal leave, sick leave, or requested leave donations.
This bill could further increase the obligations of such state agencies by an undetermined
amount dependent on the costs of hiring personnel to backfill any positions for employees using
leave provided by this bill.

FN-L817WAW-2
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 309
Committee: Ways and Means General Fund Sponsor: Representative Ginny Shaver
Analyst: John Friedenreich Date: 03/19/2024
House Bill 309 as reported by the committee on Ways and Means General Fund would decrease
the potential savings of state entities by an estimated maximum of $8,600 per employee that
utilizes eight weeks of paid leave for the birth or adoption of a child, pursuant to the provisions
of this bill, and who otherwise would have utilized unpaid leave. This bill would also provide
that the parental leave provided would not require the use of any accrued personal leave, sick
leave, or requested leave donations and would repeal current law regarding donation of leave for
maternity or adoption.
This bill could further increase the obligations of such state agencies by an undetermined
amount dependent on the costs of hiring personnel to backfill any positions for employees using
leave provided by this bill.
